rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unbelieving chiefs addressed their followers and the other people who merely imitate them, warning that following Shuʿayb would mean loss.
rows.anchor: هذه المقالة قالها الملأ لتباعهم وسائر الناس الذي يقلدونهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-rajfa is a powerful earthquake that makes a person shake, tremble, and convulse.
rows.anchor: والرجفة الزلزلة الشديدة التي ينال معها الإنسان اهتزاز وارتعاد واضطراب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author allows that one group of Shuʿayb’s people died in the earthquake and another in the cloud, or that the earthquake and cloud struck together.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل أن فرقة من قوم شعيب أهلكت ب الرجفة وفرقة بالظلة ويحتمل أن الظلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reports differ on whether Shuʿayb was sent to Midian and the people of al-Aykah as two peoples or as one people.
rows.anchor: بعث شعيبا إلى أهل مدين وإلى أصحاب الأيكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An account says that after their prolonged defiance, intense heat from a gate of Hell overcame them; a pleasant breeze and cloud drew them together, then the cloud closed over and killed them.
rows.anchor: فلما عتوا وطالت بهم المدة فتح الله عليهم بابا من أبواب جهنم فأهلكهم الحر منه

rows.speaker: عمرو بن جلهاء
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabarī reports that ʿAmr b. Jallaha saw the cloud and warned his people that Shuʿayb was a messenger and that the cloud signaled their death.
rows.anchor: أن رجلا من أهل مدين يقال له عمرو بن جلهاء قال لما رآها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The poem’s Samir and ʿImran are the people’s soothsayers, and al-Raqim is their dog.
rows.anchor: وسمير وعمران كاهناهم والرقيم كلبهم

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report says the Prophet called Shuʿayb “the orator of the prophets,” citing his words in 11:88 about not opposing his own prohibitions and seeking reform.
rows.anchor: وروي أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كان إذا ذكر «شعيبا» قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The title “orator of the prophets” refers to Shuʿayb’s graceful argument and gentle manner of address.
rows.anchor: يريد لحسن مراجعته وجميل تلطفه

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله البجلي
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabarī transmits al-Bajalī’s account that the letter-names are Midianite kings and Kulman was king at the time of the cloud.
rows.anchor: عن أبي عبد الله البجلي أنه قال: أبو جاد

rows.speaker: أخت كلمن
rows.claim: The account announces Kulman’s sister’s elegy, which says his death broke her support and that fire consumed the settlement beneath the cloud’s shade.
rows.anchor: كلمن، فقالت أخته ترثيه: [مجزوء الرمل]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author cautions that the story identifying Kulman and the other kings is speculative and God knows its truth.
rows.anchor: قال القاضي أبو محمد: وهذه حكاية مظنون بها والله علم،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase stresses how completely destruction and punishment overtook them and presents them as a lesson to others.
rows.anchor: لفظ فيه للإخبار عن قوة هلاكهم ونزول النقمة بهم والتنبيه على العبرة بهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here yaghnu means to reside and live in a place; a cited line about the route between al-Ḥajūn and al-Ṣafā illustrates the sense.
rows.anchor: ويغنوا معناه يقيموا ويسكنوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author’s survey of Arabic poetry suggests that ghani in a place denotes residence joined with comfort and a pleasant life.
rows.anchor: غنيت في المكان إنما يقال في الإقامة التي هي مقترنة بتنعم وعيش مرض

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: The line “وقد نغنى بها” is cited as evidence for the place-based sense of living amid comfortable circumstances.
rows.anchor: قول الشاعر: [الوافر] وقد نغنى بها ونرى عصورا

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: A line about neighbors who “lived” there while maintaining a pact and connection is another example of the term’s place-based usage.
rows.anchor: قول الآخر: [الرمل] ولقد يغنى بها جيرانك المس

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: The phrase “المغانيا” in a love poem is cited among poetic examples of this usage.
rows.anchor: ومنه قول الآخر: [الطويل] ألا حي من أجل الحبيب

rows.speaker: مهلهل
rows.claim: Muhalhil’s line about the family’s home in Tihama provides another example of ghani used with a place.
rows.anchor: ومنه قول مهلهل: [الخفيف] غنيت دارنا تهامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author suggests the word may derive from istighnāʾ, “being independent or self-sufficient.”
rows.anchor: ويشبه أن تكون اللفظة من الاستغناء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “As though they had not lived there yesterday” depicts them as if they had never been flourishing, thriving, and established.
rows.anchor: لأن المراد كأن لم تكن ناعمة نضرة مستقلة،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shuʿayb felt grief and compassion at his people’s destruction, since he had hoped otherwise; he recalls their rejection and his own preaching to console himself and cease mourning them.
rows.anchor: وجد في نفسه لما رأى هلاك قومه حزنا وإشفاقا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author allows that Shuʿayb may be speaking in a manner like the Prophet’s address to the people cast into the well at Badr.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل أن يقول هذه المقالة على نحو قول النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: مكي
rows.claim: Makkī says Shuʿayb and his companions left and settled in Mecca until they died there.
rows.anchor: وقال مكي: وسار شعيب بمن معه

rows.speaker: ابن وثاب وطلحة بن مصرف والأعمش
rows.claim: Ibn Waththāb, Ṭalḥa b. Muṣarrif, and al-Aʿmash read “إيسى” with kasra on the hamza, a recognized dialect form.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن وثاب وطلحة بن مصرف والأعمش: «إيسى»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This dialectal kasra pattern applies to first-person hamza, plural nūn, and second-person tāʾ, but not third-person yāʾ, according to Sībawayhi.
rows.anchor: وهذه اللغة تطرد في العلامات الثلاث، همزة التكلم

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن عمر
rows.claim: The source cites Ibn ʿUmar’s “لا أخاله” as an example of the dialectal form and says it is recorded in al-Bukhārī.
rows.anchor: قال عبد الله ابن عمر لا أخاله

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن عبد الله بن عمر
rows.claim: Ibn ʿUmar’s son is cited saying “لا أيمن” in the pilgrimage book of al-Bukhārī as a further example of the dialect.
rows.anchor: وقال ابنه عبد الله بن عبد الله بن عمر في كتاب الحج لا أيمن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author suggests that the form “ييجل” from wajila may belong to a different pattern.
rows.anchor: وأما قولهم من وجل ييجل فلعله من غير هذا الباب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Āsā means to grieve or be sorrowful.
rows.anchor: أحزن، وقرأ ابن وثاب وطلحة بن مصرف والأعمش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The form taʾadhdhana carries a sense of taking on or acquiring, based on the contrast between ʾadhina (knew, enabled) and ādhana (informed).
rows.anchor: بنية تأذن هي التي تقتضي التكسب من أذن أي علم ومكن وآذن أي أعلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When ascribed to God, the form does not imply acquiring knowledge as creatures do; it signifies knowledge as an attribute inherent in the divine essence.
rows.anchor: إذا كان مسندا إلى اسم الله عز وجل لم يلحقه معنى التكسب الذي يلحق المحدثين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author interprets the verse as “when God knew,” with the force of decisive knowledge that entails carrying the decree through; he follows Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī.
rows.anchor: فمعنى هذه الآية وإذ علم الله ليبعثن عليهم، ويقتضي قوة الكلام

rows.speaker: الطبري
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabarī and others gloss taʾadhdhana as “announced”; Ibn ʿAṭiyya calls this morphologically strained because its transitivity differs from ādhana.
rows.anchor: وقال الطبري وغيره تأذن معناه أعلم وهو قلق من جهة التصريف

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid interprets taʾadhdhana as “said”; a report also attributes to him the interpretation “commanded.”
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد: تأذن معناه قال

rows.speaker: فرقة
rows.claim: Another group interprets taʾadhdhana as “swore,” a reading the author regards as distant because the word itself does not naturally mean that.
rows.anchor: وقالت فرقة: معنى تأذن تألى.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun “upon them” refers to the Israelites who remained, not to the earlier pronoun in “for them.”
rows.anchor: والضمير في عليهم لمن بقي من بني إسرائيل لا للضمير في «لهم»

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Saʿīd b. Jubayr takes “who will subject them” as an allusion to punishment.
rows.anchor: قال سعيد بن جبير هي إشارة إلى العذاب

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās identifies the one who will subject them as Muḥammad and his community.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس هي إلى محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم وأمته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author prefers a general reference to everyone with whom the Jews have this relationship.
rows.anchor: والصحيح أنها عامة في كل من حال اليهود معه هذه الحال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yasūmuhum means to impose or burden them; the evident “painful punishment” is jizya and humiliation, and God has removed their sovereignty.
rows.anchor: ويسومهم معناه يكلفهم ويحملهم، وسوء العذاب الظاهر منه الجزية والإذلال

rows.speaker: ابن المسيب
rows.claim: Ibn al-Musayyab says Jews should be made to undergo hardship in paying the jizya.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن المسيب فيستحب أن تتعب اليهود في الجزية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says he heard that a group of Romans impoverished in their district sold neighboring Jews who lived among them and took possession of them.
rows.anchor: ولقد حدثت أن طائفة من الروم أملقت في صقعها فباعت اليهود المجاورة لهم

words: إِنَّ رَبَّكَ لَسَرِيعُ ٱلْعِقَابِ وَإِنَّهُۥ لَغَفُورٌ رَّحِيمٌ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse moves from the threat of punishment to a broad warning about God’s swift retribution, then offers mercy as reassurance and hope.
rows.anchor: ثم حسن في آخر هذه الآية لتضمنها الإيقاع بهم والوعيد أن ينبه على سرعة عقاب الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “We scattered them” means that God dispersed them throughout the earth.
rows.anchor: وقطعناهم معناه فرقناه في الأرض

rows.speaker: الطبري
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabarī transmits a group of commentators’ claim that no place on earth lacks a community of Jews.
rows.anchor: قال الطبري عن جماعة من المفسرين: ما في الأرض بقعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people intended are apparently the Israelites after Solomon, when their kingdom ended.
rows.anchor: والظاهر في المشار إليهم في هذه الآية أنهم الذين بعد سليمان وقت زوال ملكهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author places this period before Jesus, since after rejecting Jesus the Israelites had no righteous people.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أنه قبل مدة عيسى عليه السلام لأنه لم يكن فيهم صالح بعد كفرهم بعيسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Historical accounts about this period are inconsistent and confused.
rows.anchor: وفي التواريخ في هذا الفصل روايات مضطربة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If ṣalāḥ means faith, dūna dhālika means those other than believers, namely disbelievers.
rows.anchor: أن يدعها صلاح الإيمان ف دون بمعنى غير يراد بها الكفرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If ṣalāḥ means worship, goodness, and their implications of faith, dūna dhālika may include believers who fall short of that degree.
rows.anchor: وإن أريد بالصلاح العبادة والخير وتوابع الإيمان ف دون ذلك يحتمل أن يكون في مؤمنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Balawnāhum means “We tested them.”
rows.anchor: وبلوناهم معناه امتحناهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The good things are health, prosperity, and the like as people ordinarily regard them; the bad things are their opposites.
rows.anchor: وبالحسنات الصحة والرخاء ونحو هذا مما هو بحسب رأي ابن آدم ونظره،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “So that they might return” is phrased from the human observer’s perspective and means returning to obedience and repenting of sin.
rows.anchor: وقوله: لعلهم أي بحسب رأيكم لو شاهدتم ذلك

words: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ تَدْعُونَ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ
rows.speaker: جمهور الناس
rows.claim: The majority read inna with a geminated nūn and ʿibād in the nominative; the address belittles idols as created, material bodies that are themselves subject to worship or ownership.
rows.anchor: قرأ جمهور الناس «إن الذين تدعون من دون الله عباد أمثالكم»

words: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ تَدْعُونَ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ
rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Maqātil says the verse addresses a group of Khuzaʿa who worshipped angels, informing them that angels are servants like them, not gods.
rows.anchor: وقال مقاتل، إن المراد بهذه الآية طائفة من العرب

words: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ تَدْعُونَ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ
rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Saʿīd b. Jubayr reads the nūn of in lightly and puts ʿibādan and amthālakum in the accusative: in means “not,” denying that idols are servants like humans.
rows.anchor: وقرأ سعيد بن جبير «إن الذين تدعون من دون الله عبادا أمثالكم»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On Saʿīd b. Jubayr’s reading, the idols are less and baser than humans because they are inert and cannot understand or reason.
rows.anchor: بل هم أقل وأحقر إذ هي جمادات لا تفهم ولا تعقل

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: Sībawayhi says in meaning mā is too weak to govern the predicate, so it remains nominative; this is the grammatical form he considers correct for the reading.
rows.anchor: وسيبويه يرى أن «إن» إذا كانت بمعنى «ما» فإنها تضعف

rows.speaker: أبو العباس المبرد
rows.claim: Al-Mubarrad permits in when it means mā to govern like mā and put its predicate in the accusative.
rows.anchor: وأبو العباس المبرد يجيز أن تعمل عمل «ما» في نصب الخبر

words: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ تَدْعُونَ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ
rows.speaker: الكسائي
rows.claim: Al-Kisāʾī says in meaning mā only occurs with illā, as in 67:2.
rows.anchor: وزعم الكسائي أن «إن» بمعنى «ما» لا تجيء إلا وبعدها إلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command is a test: call the idols, and if they do not answer, that confirms the description just given.
rows.anchor: ثم بين تعالى الحجة بقوله فادعوهم أي فاختبروا فإن لم يستجيبوا فهم كما وصفنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The questions ask whether idols have the senses and capacities of living creatures; denying these details forces assent to the broader conclusion that they are inert.
rows.anchor: الغرض من هذه الآية، ألهم حواس الحي وأوصافه؟

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Breaking the general claim into specific faculties makes the proof stronger and leaves no room for doubt.
rows.anchor: فإذا وقع الإقرار بتفصيلات القضية لزم الإقرار بعمومها وكان بيانها أقوى

rows.speaker: الزهراوي
rows.claim: Al-Zahrawī says the worshippers themselves are superior to the idols because they possess useful limbs, so they should not worship them.
rows.anchor: قال الزهراوي: المعنى أنتم أفضل منهم بهذه الجوارح النافعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Saʿīd b. Jubayr’s reading, understood as negation, entails that idols are not servants like human beings.
rows.anchor: قال القاضي أبو محمد: و «تتقون» بهذا التأويل قراءة سعيد بن جبير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Each am in the questions turns away from the preceding clause; it is not the alternative am paired with alif when asking which of two things is present.
rows.anchor: وقوله في الآية أم إضراب لكل واحدة عن الجملة المتقدمة لها،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author calls the distinction semantic; in wording and grammatical analysis, both kinds of am are the same.
rows.anchor: وهذا عندي فرق معنوي، وأما من جهة اللفظ والصناعة النحوية

rows.speaker: نافع والحسن والأعرج
rows.claim: Nāfiʿ, al-Ḥasan, and al-Aʿraj read yabṭishūna with kasra on the ṭāʾ.
rows.anchor: وقرأ نافع والحسن والأعرج «يبطشون» بكسر الطاء

rows.speaker: نافع وأبو جعفر وشيبة
rows.claim: Nāfiʿ, Abū Jaʿfar, and Shayba also transmit yabṭushūna with ḍamma on the ṭāʾ.
rows.anchor: وقرأ نافع أيضا وأبو جعفر وشيبة «يبطشون» بضمها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God commands the Prophet to challenge them to summon the idols to harm or plot against him, and not delay; if they are gods, their action should become evident.
rows.anchor: ثم أمر الله تعالى نبيه صلى الله عليه وسلم أن يعجزهم بقوله قل ادعوا شركاءكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They are called “partners” because the people assigned them a relation to themselves by naming them gods and partners of God.
rows.anchor: وسماهم شركاءهم من حيث لهم نسبة إليهم بتسميتهم إياهم آلهة وشركاء لله

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو ونافع
rows.claim: Abū ʿAmr and Nāfiʿ retain the yāʾ in kaydūnī when connecting the words.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو ونافع «كيدوني» بإثبات الياء في الوصل،

rows.speaker: ابن كثير وعاصم وابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي
rows.claim: Ibn Kathīr, ʿĀṣim, Ibn ʿĀmir, Ḥamza, and al-Kisāʾī omit the yāʾ in both connection and pause.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير وعاصم وابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي «كيدون» بحذف الياء

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Abū ʿAlī explains that yāʾ deletion is common when speech resembles a separate phrase or a rhyme, as in al-Aʿshā’s verse ending with an omitted yāʾ.
rows.anchor: قال أبو علي: إذا أشبه الكلام المنفصل أو كان منفصلا أشبه القافية

rows.speaker: الأعشى
rows.claim: Al-Aʿshā’s line “أن يأتين” illustrates omission of the final yāʾ in rhyme.
rows.anchor: كما قال الأعشى: [المتقارب] فهل يمنعني ارتيادي البلا

rows.speaker: الأعشى
rows.claim: A second al-Aʿshā line, “يلمس الأحلاس,” illustrates omission of the yāʾ that marks the imperative.
rows.anchor: كما قال الأعشى: [الرمل] يلمس الأحلاس في منزله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Falayunẓirūn means “do not delay me”; the author links it with the same sense of naẓara in 2:280.
rows.anchor: وقوله فلا تنظرون أي لا تؤخرون، ومنه قوله تعالى: فنظرة

none: A bare heading with no commentary.

rows.speaker: الطبري وغيره
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabarī and others report that at Mecca the Companions talked during obligatory prayer about their needs, called out at verses of mercy or punishment, and asked one another whether they had prayed and how much remained.
rows.anchor: ذكر الطبري وغيره أن سبب هذه الآية هو أن أصحاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كانوا بمكة يتكلمون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects the view that this verse concerns the sermon because it is Meccan and sermons began only after the Prophet’s migration; he also rejects al-Zahrawī’s report of a young Anṣārī reciting while the Prophet recited.
rows.anchor: وأما قول من قال إنها في الخطبة فضعيف، لأن الآية مكية،

rows.speaker: الزهراوي
rows.claim: Al-Zahrawī reports that the occasion was a young Anṣārī reciting during prayer while the Prophet recited; the author groups this report with the weak sermon explanation.
rows.anchor: وكذلك ما ذكر الزهراوي أنها نزلت بسبب فتى من الأنصار كان يقرأ في الصلاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muslims unanimously must stop speaking and listen in prayer.
rows.anchor: فأما الاستماع والإنصات عن الكلام في الصلاة فإجماع

rows.speaker: فرقة
rows.claim: One group says a follower must refrain from reciting altogether, whether the imam recites aloud or silently.
rows.anchor: فقالت فرقة: يمسك المأموم عن القراءة جملة

rows.speaker: فرقة
rows.claim: Another group says a follower recites when the imam is silent and refrains when the imam recites aloud.
rows.anchor: وقالت فرقة: يقرأ المأموم إذا أسر الإمام

rows.speaker: فرقة
rows.claim: A third group says that during loud recitation the follower refrains from the sūra but recites the opening sūra, al-Fātiḥa.
rows.anchor: وقالت فرقة: يسمك المأموم في جهر الإمام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author favors the third position and says sound Prophetic reports support it; he does not fully review disagreements because the verse’s wording does not address recitation behind the imam.
rows.anchor: قال القاضي أبو محمد: ومع هذا القول أحاديث صحاح عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse requires silence from speech in prayer; silence during the sermon is established by sunna, while the verse applies if Qurʾān is recited in the sermon. Outside prayer, listening is recommended, but honoring the Qurʾān is obligatory in every state.
rows.anchor: فهذه الآية واجبة الحكم في الصلاة أن ينصت عن الحديث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Inṣāt means silence.
rows.anchor: والإنصات السكوت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The closing phrase expresses the human hope of receiving mercy.
rows.anchor: ولعلكم على ترجي البشر

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Saʿīd b. Jubayr says the command to listen includes the days of the two feasts and Friday, as well as the imam’s loud recitation in prayer.
rows.anchor: وذكر الطبري عن سعيد بن جبير أنه قال في قوله عز وجل

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj says the command may mean to act according to the Qurʾān and not transgress it.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج: ويجوز أن يكون فاستمعوا له وأنصتوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address to the Prophet extends to the whole community and commands remembrance, glorification, praise, and sanctification of God.
rows.anchor: مخاطبة للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم تعم جميع أمته وهو أمر من الله عز وجل بذكره وتسبيحه

rows.speaker: جمهور
rows.claim: The majority hold that remembrance “within oneself” still requires movement of the tongue, as indicated by “below the loudness of speech.”
rows.anchor: والجمهور على أن الذكر لا يكون في النفس ولا يراعى إلا بحركة اللسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase describes the level of quiet, spoken remembrance rather than silent thought.
rows.anchor: فهذه مرتبة السر والمخافتة باللفظ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taḍarruʿan means humility and submission.
rows.anchor: وتضرعا معناه تذللا وخضوعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khīfatan derives from khawfatan, with wāw changed to yāʾ because of the preceding kasra.
rows.anchor: وخيفة أصلها خوفة بدلت الواو ياء لأجل الكسرة التي تقدمتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase means to remember God continually, every day, and at the day’s two ends.
rows.anchor: وقوله بالغدو والآصال معناه دأبا وفي كل يوم

rows.speaker: فرقة
rows.claim: One group says the verse describes Muslim prayer before the five daily prayers were made obligatory.
rows.anchor: وقالت فرقة هذه الآية كانت في صلاة المسلمين قبل فرض الصلوات الخمس

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda identifies al-ghudu as the dawn prayer and al-āṣāl as the afternoon prayer.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة: «الغدو» صلاة الصبح والآصال صلاة العصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-āṣāl is a plural of aṣl, itself a plural of aṣīl, and may also be a direct plural of aṣīl or a plural of a plural, like īmān from yamīn.
rows.anchor: والآصال جمع أصل والأصل جمع أصيل وهو العشي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author reports Abū Majliz’s reading “والإيصال” as a verbal noun parallel to “الإصباح” and “الإمساء,” meaning entry into late afternoon.
rows.anchor: «والإيصال» مصدر كالإصباح والإمساء

rows.speaker: أبو وائل
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabarī transmits Abū Wāʾil asking his servant, “Have we entered evening yet?” as an example of the verb aṣala.
rows.anchor: وفي الطبري قال أبو وائل لغلامه هل آصلنا بعد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After warning against heedlessness, God gives the angels as an example of exertion to encourage earnest obedience.
rows.anchor: ولما قال الله عز وجل ولا تكن من الغافلين جعل بعد ذلك مثالا من اجتهاد الملائكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Those who are with your Lord” refers to the angels.
rows.anchor: وقوله الذين يريد الملائكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their being “with” God means rank, honor, and nearness in status, not physical location.
rows.anchor: وقوله عند إنما يريد في المنزلة والتشريف والقرب في المكانة لا في المكان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels are humble and persist in worship, glorification, and prostration.
rows.anchor: ثم وصف تعالى حالهم من تواضعهم وإدمانهم للعبادة والتسبيح والسجود

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A Prophetic report says the sky groans, rightly, because no space the size of a handspan is without a standing, bowing, or prostrating angel.
rows.anchor: وفي الحديث: أطت السماء وحق لها أن تئط ما فيها موضع شبر إلا وفيه ملك

rows.speaker: النخعي
rows.claim: Al-Nakhaʿī, in the book of al-Naqqāsh, says one may either bow or prostrate at this verse’s prostration marker.
rows.anchor: قال النخعي في كتاب النقاش: إن شئت ركعت وإن شئت سجدت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This opens a report and divine judgment: the hypocrite men and women share the same status and degree of unbelief, as “ears are part of the head” describes shared legal treatment for wiping.
rows.anchor: هذا ابتداء إخبار عنهم وحكم من الله تعالى عليهم بما تضمنته الآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earlier statement “they are not of you” makes this declaration appropriate; the author compares it with the legal expression that the ears are part of the head for wiping.
rows.anchor: وهذا نحو قولهم الأذنان من الرأس يريدون في حكم المسح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their enjoining evil means calling to unbelief, worship of other than God, and the other evils named in the verse.
rows.anchor: وقوله يأمرون بالمنكر يريد بالكفر وعبادة غير الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These hypocrites lacked power and overt public actions because Islam and God’s word had become dominant.
rows.anchor: لأن المنافقين الذين نزلت هذه الآيات فيهم لم يكونوا أهل قدرة ولا أفعال ظاهرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their “withholding hands” refers to withholding charity and good works.
rows.anchor: و «القبض» هو عن الصدقة وفعل الخير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They forgot God by abandoning His Prophet and law; God then left them without guidance or protection from Hell’s punishment.
rows.anchor: أي تركوه حين تركوا نبيه وشرعته فتركهم حين لم يهدهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling divine abandonment “forgetting” intensifies the sense of leaving them, as abandonment has reached the degree associated with forgetfulness.
rows.anchor: وإنما يعبر بالنسيان عن الترك مبالغة إذا بلغ وجوه الترك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author compares this sense of nisyān as abandonment with 2:237 and 28:77.
rows.anchor: وعلى هذا يجيء ولا تنسوا الفضل بينكم [البقرة: 237]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their fisq is the unbelief that entails eternal residence in Hell.
rows.anchor: ثم حكم عليهم عز وجل بالفسق وهو فسوق الكفر المقتضي للخلود في النار

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda says God left them out of good, but did not leave them out of evil.
rows.anchor: وكان قتادة يقول فنسيهم أي من الخير ولم ينسهم من الشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Specifying that the promise concerns evil makes a pure threat appropriate and well worded.
rows.anchor: لما قيد الوعد بالتصريح بالشر صح ذلك وحسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The “disbelievers” here are those who openly declare unbelief.
rows.anchor: والكفار في هذه الآية المعلنون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fire is sufficient for them as recompense and punishment for their crime and unbelief; even a wish for further punishment would find enough in it.
rows.anchor: أي كافيتهم وكافية جرمهم وكفرهم نكالا وجزاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s curse means that He has driven them away from His mercy.
rows.anchor: ولعنهم الله معناه أبعدهم عن رحمته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lasting punishment is eternal and admits no transfer away from it.
rows.anchor: وعذاب مقيم معناه مؤبد لا نقلة له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God tells the Prophet to address the hypocrites as like the peoples who came before them, or as having the same example.
rows.anchor: أمر الله نبيه أن يخاطب بها المنافقين فيقول لهم كالذين من قبلكم

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj proposes that the phrase means “a promise like that made to those before you,” attaching it to “God promised”; the author calls this strained in the continuation.
rows.anchor: وقال الزجاج: المعنى وعدا كما وعد الذين من قبلكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects al-Zajjāj’s attachment of the phrase to “God promised” as strained; the direct sense is that earlier peoples were stronger and richer yet disobeyed and were destroyed, so the hypocrites are more liable to destruction.
rows.anchor: قال القاضي أبو محمد: وهذا قلق، ثم قال كانوا أشد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khallāq is a person’s allotted share, religion, and overall condition, what is fitting for that person.
rows.anchor: والخلاق الحظ من القدر والدين وجميع حال المرء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earlier peoples hastened to take their worldly share and abandoned the Hereafter; the hypocrites followed them.
rows.anchor: والمعنى عجلوا حظهم في دنياهم وتركوا باب الآخرة

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabarī cites the Prophetic report that later people will follow earlier peoples step by step, even into a lizard’s hole; the author says it does not fit this verse, which addresses unbelieving hypocrites, whereas the report addresses monotheists copying worldly practices that do not expel them from religion.
rows.anchor: وأورد الطبري في تفسير هذه الآية قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم «لتتبعن سنن من قبلكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khudtum means you mixed or plunged into the same matters as they did; it is borrowed from moving through liquids and is used for falsehood, whose affairs are disordered rather than systematic.
rows.anchor: وقوله خضتم كالذي خاضوا أي خلطتم كالذي خلطوا،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says khawḍ is used only of falsehood, since truth is handled in ordered fashion while false matters are muddled.
rows.anchor: ولا يستعمل إلا في الباطل، لأن التصرف في الحقائق إنما هو

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet’s warning that someone who misappropriates God’s wealth will enter the Fire is cited as an example of khawḍ in wrongdoing.
rows.anchor: ومنه قول النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم «رب متخوض في مال الله له النار يوم القيامة»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One possible referent for “those” is the earlier peoples described as powerful and wealthy: the hypocrites likewise lose their works through turning away from truth.
rows.anchor: فيحتمل أن يراد ب أولئك القوم الذين وصفهم بالشدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, “those” refers to Muḥammad’s contemporary hypocrites, with a shift of address to the Prophet.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل أن يريد ب أولئك المنافقين المعاصرين لمحمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥabiṭa describes work becoming void after the effort has been expended; ḥabaṭa also names a belly illness, with fatḥa on the bāʾ.
rows.anchor: و «حبط العمل» وما جرى مجراه يحبط حبطا إذا بطل بعد التعب فيه

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A Prophetic report says that some plants of spring can kill by ḥabaṭ or nearly do so, illustrating the word for the belly illness.
rows.anchor: ومنه قول النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم «إن مما ينبت الربيع ما يقتل حبطا أو يلم»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In this life, hypocrites incur believers’ contempt and have their affairs spoiled; in the Hereafter their works bring neither benefit nor reward.
rows.anchor: في الدنيا معناه إذا كان في المنافقين ما يصيبهم في الدنيا من المقت من المؤمنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The following verse’s opening, “Has there not come to them,” strengthens the interpretation that “those” means the contemporary hypocrites.
rows.anchor: ويقوي أن الإشارة ب أولئك إلى المنافقين قوله في الآية المستقبلة ألم يأتهم

none: A bare heading with no commentary.
